content.title: About
content.content: Frozen margarita is a ready‑to‑serve frozen cocktail made with tequila, lime juice, and triple sec. It delivers the refreshing sweet‑tart flavor of a classic margarita in a convenient, freezer‑stable format.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frozen margarita is often sold in single‑serve packets, perfect for travel and picnics.
The drink retains the bright lime aroma and tequila notes even after freezing.
Many versions include a salted rim option to mimic the traditional serving style.
Freezing allows manufacturers to control sugar levels, often using natural sweeteners.
Frozen margarita can be used as a base for dessert cocktails by adding fruit or ice cream.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Lime juice provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many alcoholic drinks, frozen margarita typically contains very little fat.

items.title: Moderate calorie content
items.content: When choosing a low‑sugar brand and consuming in moderation, frozen margarita can be less caloric than a traditional sugary cocktail.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: The high water content of the frozen drink helps maintain hydration, especially on hot days.

items.title: Contains a modest amount of tequila
items.content: Moderate tequila intake may promote relaxation and improve mood.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Frozen margarita contains alcohol and should not be consumed by minors, pregnant women, or individuals taking medications that interact with alcohol.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some brands add sugar, increasing calories and potentially affecting blood glucose levels.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Lime can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Cold sensitivity
items.content: Consuming a very cold beverage may cause tooth or throat discomfort.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Remove the packet from the freezer, let it soften for 5‑10 minutes, then blend or shake until smooth. Serve in a glass with a salted rim and garnish with a lime wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen margarita in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once opened, use within 1‑2 months. Do not store at room temperature, as it will melt and lose quality.
